title: Cheesy Polenta Bowls with Tomato-Basil White Beans, Spinach & Roasted Zucchini
summary: Creamy quick-cooking polenta with mozzarella, topped with tomato-basil white beans and spinach, alongside roasted zucchini. A balanced, meat-free dairy dinner in about 35 minutes (25 minutes active).
ingredients: 1 cup quick-cooking polenta (not traditional long-cooking cornmeal)
2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1/2 tsp dried basil (or 2 tbsp fresh basil)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss zucchini half-moons with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 18–22 minutes, turning once, until tender and lightly browned.

Meanwhile heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook 3–4 minutes. Stir in garlic for 30 seconds, then add halved cherry tomatoes, oregano, basil and a pinch of salt. Cook 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes soften and release juices. Add 2–3 tbsp water if dry.
Stir drained white beans into tomato skillet and warm for 3–4 minutes. Add chopped spinach and stir 1–2 minutes until wilted. Finish with optional lemon juice; keep warm on low.

In a saucepan bring 3 cups water and 1 cup milk to a gentle boil. Whisk in 1 cup quick-cooking polenta gradually, reduce heat to low and cook according to package directions (usually 3–5 minutes), stirring often. Remove from heat and stir in mozzarella and salt. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Spoon polenta into bowls. Top adults’ portions with white beans, tomato and spinach. Serve roasted zucchini alongside. For kids, offer components separately.
child_friendly_modifications: Serve a small bowl of cheesy polenta with plain warmed white beans on the side, a few sweet roasted zucchini pieces, and tomato sauce as an optional topping. For the 3-year-old, mash or flatten beans if needed and cut zucchini into soft bite-sized pieces. Allow hot polenta to cool before serving.
leftovers: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours. Store polenta separately from beans and vegetables for up to 3–4 days. Reheat polenta with a splash of water or milk over low heat, stirring until creamy; warm the bean mixture thoroughly. Alternatively, chill leftover polenta in a shallow dish, cut into squares and pan-sear for lunch with leftover beans.
